We scored major points in three of the five field events with our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, winning both the Shot and Discus, and young A.
A. Bergvalds, our Latvian member, scored points for us in the Weight Put and Discus Throw, but we missed the help of Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw.

Underwood was second in the 440 and Bill Lucas scored a good win over Len Herbert in the 2 miles run when clocking 9 mins. 39 secs. A. Bergvalds, our Latvian member, won the weight and discus events and Terry Bateman won the javelin throw.
Vernon Blowfield won the 2 miles run and A. Bergvalds won the discus and was second in the weight, but on the whole we did not do so well as expected.

Birch, and as the second and third men home were foreigners, Charlie missed a fine chance of being the second Englishman to finish. Our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, competed in the Discus event but failed to reach the standard of 125 feet.
A. Bergvalds retained his Weight and Discus titles and Charlie Melchior once again won the Javelin Throw.
Alan Law won the Shot Put handicap with the scratch man, A. Bergvalds, in second place and Bert Machell who was third also won the Hop, Step and Jump handicap.

Hall, who is quite a promising youngster, finished second, with Syd Jarlett holding off Harry Shields down the straight to take third place. A. Bergvalds, our Latvian member, set up a new club record in the Shot Putt with 41 ft. 5 ins., and won the handicap from the scratch mark.

Ans Bergvalds was undoubtedly our best performer. His Club Championship record of 125 ft. 7 ins. in the Discus, added to which in the Boxing Day handicap he put the Shot 41 ft. 5ins.—the best performance ever by a Club member—were most gratifying.

Much of the credit must go to our field event men, who, taking Charlie Jones' winter " pep " talks to heart, gained 32 out of a possible 40 points. A. Bergvalds had a great day, winning the weight with 42 ft. 3 ins.

Bob Taylor was second in the 1 mile, with Reg Bolam in fourth place, and Len Adams was second in the 2 miles run, with George Durrant in third place. A. Bergvalds won the high jump, an unusual event for him, but as he cleared 5 ft. 5 ins. he is thus a decided asset to our jumping ranks.

In the straight running events we did well, with Jack Brown winning the half-mile, Reg Bolam taking the 1 mile and Bill Lucas the 3 miles, with Les Stokell in second place. A. Bergvalds won the weight and was second in the discus, while P.
Ray Tooby was second in the 1 mile and Les Stokell was runner-up to Alec Olney in the 2 miles run. A. Bergvalds was second in the high jump and also gained a double victory in the weight and discus.

Walker was third in the 1 mile and Bill Lucas occupied a similar place in the 3 miles. Eddie Short was second in the 2 miles steeplechase, and A. Bergvalds was second in the weight and third in the discus throw.
